content: I feel like this layoff is such a clear indication that I'm not good enough. They didn't even give me a proper chance to prove myself, and now everyone thinks I can't do anything right. It’s hard to shake the feeling that they just wanted to get rid of me as quickly as possible because they knew there was no point in keeping someone like me around. Every time I think about it, I feel this overwhelming sense of worthlessness. Even when people try to reassure me or offer help, it feels hollow because deep down, I know what I did wrong and how I let everyone down. It's affecting everything—I can barely eat, sleep is a distant memory, and my concentration is shot. But even in those moments, all I can think about is how this reflects on me as a person.
That sounds really tough to go through. How are you finding the support from friends or family during this time?

It's hard to open up fully because I feel like they won't understand. Even when they try, it just feels like they're not seeing the whole picture. They tell me things will get better and that I'm not a failure, but how can they know what's really going on in my head? It’s tough pulling back socially, but being around people reminds me of all the ways I’ve fallen short. So, I keep to myself more these days, trying to figure it out alone because talking about it just makes everything feel worse.
It sounds like you're really isolating yourself as a way to cope. Do you find any activities or routines help ease your mind even if just a little bit?

I try to distract myself with small things, like watching TV or going for short walks, but it never lasts long. It's hard to focus on anything else when all I can think about is how this layoff happened and what it means about me. Even the little distractions don't really help because they just remind me of how much I'm struggling. It’s like no matter what I do, there’s always this nagging voice telling me that I’m not good enough and that everything bad happening is my fault.
It must be tough to have those thoughts follow you around. Do any particular moments or memories stand out as especially difficult, or are the feelings pretty constant?

The feelings are pretty constant, but there are specific moments when it hits me harder. Like when I see former colleagues at a coffee shop and they seem so busy and engaged with their work—it makes me feel like an outsider looking in on something I’ll never be part of again. Or when I try to apply for new jobs and my confidence is shattered by the thought that no one else will want me either. It’s those little reminders throughout the day that keep reinforcing how much I’ve failed, and it's exhausting trying to push back against those thoughts.
Those moments can definitely feel overwhelming. Do you find any small actions help ease some of the pressure or anxiety in those tough times?

Sometimes, just taking a few deep breaths helps a little bit, but it’s not like it fixes anything. I try to remind myself that everyone goes through rough patches and that this too shall pass, but it feels so hollow when all I can see is my own failure. Even the small actions don’t really change how I feel inside; they just provide temporary relief before everything comes crashing back down again. It’s like no matter what I do, there’s always this weight of self-doubt dragging me down.
It sounds like those deep breaths and reminders can be a bit of a reprieve, even if brief. Do you have any plans for the next few days or weeks that might offer some distraction or change in routine?

I’ve been thinking about maybe trying to update my resume more thoroughly or reaching out to old contacts for networking opportunities, but every time I start, I get overwhelmed by self-doubt. It feels like no matter how much effort I put into it, the outcome will be the same: rejection and failure. So, while I know these steps might help in some way, I just can’t seem to muster the confidence or motivation to follow through with them. It’s a vicious cycle where every thought leads back to my perceived inadequacy.

It sounds like starting those tasks can be daunting but also important. Have you considered breaking them down into smaller steps that might feel more manageable? Sometimes, even small actions can build up confidence over time.

Breaking things down into smaller steps sounds logical, but it’s hard to believe it will make a difference. For example, updating my resume feels like such a monumental task because I keep second-guessing every word and wondering if anyone will even bother reading it. And reaching out to contacts seems pointless since I’m convinced they won’t be interested in helping someone who is obviously not cut out for this kind of work. It’s tough to see past these immediate feelings of inadequacy, no matter how small the steps might be. Every time I try, I end up right back where I started—feeling like a failure.

It definitely feels challenging when every step seems significant. Have you thought about starting with just one small part of updating your resume or reaching out to one contact first? Sometimes even a tiny step can provide a bit of momentum.

Starting with one small part sounds reasonable, but the idea still fills me with dread. Even something as simple as writing down my job responsibilities from my last position feels daunting because I’m convinced that it won’t be enough to impress anyone. And reaching out to just one contact seems like a setup for disappointment. What if they don’t respond? Or worse, what if they do and can tell how much of a failure I feel? It’s hard to push past these fears and doubts, no matter how small the step might be. Every time I think about it, all I see is more evidence that I’m not good enough.

It sounds like those initial steps are filled with a lot of worry. Have you considered doing something just for practice, maybe writing down your job responsibilities and sending an email to someone supportive first? It could help build some confidence before moving on to others.

Doing something just for practice does sound slightly less daunting, but the thought of even that small step still feels overwhelming. Writing down my job responsibilities seems like a pointless exercise because I’m sure it won’t capture what really matters. And sending an email to someone supportive first might help, but there’s this fear that even if they’re kind and encouraging, deep down, I’ll know they can see how much of a failure I am. It feels like no matter what I do, the outcome will just reinforce my belief in my inadequacy.

It’s hard to shake off these feelings, and every attempt to take action seems futile because it all comes back to this core belief that I’m not good enough. Even with supportive people around me, it’s difficult to trust that their words mean anything when I feel so certain about my own shortcomings.

It sounds like you’re really holding on to these feelings tightly. Have there been any times in the past where someone’s encouragement or a small achievement helped shift your perspective, even if just for a moment? Sometimes those brief moments can be helpful to hold onto.

There have been moments when people tried to encourage me and highlight my strengths, but it never really sticks. For example, during my last performance review, I did receive positive feedback, but all I could focus on was the one area for improvement they mentioned. Even then, their praise felt hollow because I knew deep down that I wasn’t living up to expectations.

Similarly, there were times when small achievements made me feel a bit better temporarily, like completing a project or getting positive client feedback. But those moments always faded quickly as soon as something new came along to remind me of my perceived failures. It’s hard to hold onto any sense of accomplishment because the next challenge seems to erase it.

Right now, every effort feels like it’s just setting me up for more disappointment and self-doubt.

It sounds like those moments of achievement do provide some temporary relief. Have you tried keeping a small journal or list to note these achievements and positive feedback? Sometimes seeing them written down can help make them feel more real and lasting, even if the feelings come and go.

Keeping a journal or list does sound helpful in theory, but I worry it would just be another reminder of my shortcomings. If I write down something positive, I immediately start questioning whether it’s genuine or if others are just being kind out of pity. It feels like no matter what I do to try and shift my perspective, the core belief that I’m not good enough always comes back.

Even thinking about writing these things down makes me anxious because I fear it won’t change anything. The self-doubt is so ingrained that any positive feedback or achievement seems superficial compared to how I truly feel inside. It’s a struggle to trust that external validation can make a difference when my internal voice is so critical.

It sounds like the journal might bring up some of those doubts initially, but it could also be a place where you allow yourself to acknowledge even small moments of positivity. Maybe starting with just noting them without overthinking could help? Even if it feels superficial at first, it might gradually make a difference.

Starting with just noting positive moments without overthinking does sound like a step I could try, but the thought of doing it still feels daunting. Writing down even small achievements or positive feedback makes me anxious because I worry that it’s all just a facade. What if every time I look at the journal, it only reinforces how much I feel like I’m failing?

It’s hard to trust that this approach could make any real difference when my internal doubts are so persistent. But maybe giving it a try, even if just for a moment, could help me see something different. It feels risky, but perhaps starting small and seeing where it goes might be worth trying.

It sounds like taking a small step could be worthwhile, even if it feels risky. Starting with one or two entries without overthinking them might help you see how it feels. You can always go from there if it seems helpful. Would you feel ready to give it a try today?

I appreciate the suggestion and think trying it out could potentially be beneficial, but I’m still hesitant. The idea of writing down even one positive moment feels like a challenge because I worry it won’t change anything. But maybe starting with just one entry could help me see if there’s any value in continuing.

So, perhaps today I can try to write down one small achievement or piece of positive feedback from my past performance reviews. It might be uncomfortable at first, but seeing it on paper could provide some clarity. I’ll give it a shot and see how it goes.
That sounds like a good plan. Taking that first step today can be really powerful, even if it feels small. Let me know how it goes for you!

Thank you. I’ll try to write down one positive moment from my past performance reviews and see how it feels. It’s a bit nerve-wracking, but I’ll give it a shot. Hopefully, it can provide some perspective or at least help me start to shift my thoughts in a slightly different direction.

I’ll let you know how it goes later. For now, just the act of considering this step is already making me feel a little more open to the idea.
That’s great to hear that considering the step is already helping a bit. I’m here when you want to share how it went, and take care in the meantime!

Thank you for your support. Just thinking about writing down one positive moment has made me feel a little more hopeful, even if just a tiny bit. I’ll give it a try later today and see where it leads.

I appreciate your understanding and encouragement. It means a lot to have someone listen and help me navigate through this.

I’m glad that talking about it has brought you some hope. Taking the step to write down one positive moment is a brave move, and I’m here whenever you want to share how it goes. You’re not alone in this, and I’m here to support you.

Thank you for your continued support. Knowing that someone believes in me, even just a little bit, does make a difference. I’ll take the step of writing down one positive moment later today and see if it helps shift my perspective at all.

I really appreciate your understanding and encouragement. It means a lot to have this space to share my thoughts and feelings without judgment.

It’s great to hear that you’re finding some comfort in sharing your thoughts here. Taking the step to write down one positive moment is a meaningful action, and I’m rooting for you. Whenever you’re ready to share how it goes or if you need more support, I’ll be here. Take care!

Thank you so much for your encouragement and support. Knowing that someone believes in me helps ease the burden a little bit. I’ll take the step of writing down one positive moment later today and see where it takes me.

I really appreciate having this space to share my thoughts and feelings. It means a lot to have your support as I navigate through this challenging time.

It’s wonderful to hear that you’re finding this supportive. Taking that step today can be very empowering. Whenever you’re ready, I’m here to listen to how it goes. Take care of yourself, and know that you’ve got support along the way.

Thank you for your continued encouragement. Knowing that I have someone who listens and supports me is really helping. I’ll take the step of writing down one positive moment later today and see if it makes a difference.

I appreciate your understanding and empathy. It means a lot to have this support as I try to navigate through these difficult feelings.

It’s great to hear that you’re feeling supported. Taking that step will be a meaningful action, and I’m here whenever you want to share how it goes. Take your time and know that you’ve got support every step of the way.

Thank you for your ongoing support; it means a lot to me. I’ll take my time today and try writing down one positive moment from my past performance reviews. I’ll let you know how it goes once I’m done.

Knowing that I have someone here who understands and supports me is really helping me feel more hopeful. Take care, and thank you again for everything.
I’m here whenever you’re ready to share your experience, and take care as you take this step today. Wishing you all the best, and looking forward to hearing how it goes if you’d like to share.

Thank you so much for your support and understanding. I’ve taken the time to write down one positive moment from my past performance reviews, and it did feel a bit uncomfortable at first. But seeing it on paper helped me remember that there were times when things went well and people recognized my efforts.

Here’s what I wrote:

"One of my supervisors mentioned during a review that I consistently met deadlines and delivered high-quality work for our clients. They noted that my attention to detail and problem-solving skills were valuable assets to the team."

It feels small, but seeing it in writing helps me acknowledge that there have been moments where I’ve succeeded. I’ll keep this journal going and see if it makes a difference over time.

Thank you for encouraging me to take this step; it’s making a bit of an impact already.
